Banishing Light: Premium white removal and a first-pickable catch-all for any nonland permanent, plus it turns on Builder's Talent. The 55.8% GIH is dampened by its sorcery speed (LR's caveat: don't take it over curve early), but exiling their best thing reliably is exactly what removal-scarce BLB wants.
Beza, the Bounding Spring: Colorless-agnostic white bomb: a 4/5 for four that almost always cashes in multiple modes (life, Fish, Treasure, card) against a developed board. 62.6% GIH with a 1.5 ALSA and +9.3 IWD — first-pick material in any white deck, no synergy required.
Brave-Kin Duo: Filler. A 1/1 for W whose repeatable sorcery-speed pump is too slow to matter; the negative IWD and 52% GIH mean it's doing nothing when drawn late. A curve-filler body for RW/GW Mice-Rabbits go-wide only, and even there it's near the bottom of the deck.
Brightblade Stoat: Solid aggro two-drop and near-format-defining glue for any white beatdown deck (RW Mice, GW Rabbits). First strike + lifelink means it trades up, races, and blunts opposing aggro; 57.9% GIH on an 89% play rate with early ALSA 2.8 confirms it as a reliable early pick, not a synergy card.
Builder's Talent: Solid GW/white playable the C grade undersells — LR loves it (A/A+), and 56.8% GIH with +3.5 IWD backs that. The 0/4 Wall blocks the format's aggro while noncreature permanents (Talents, Food, Auras, Season) print counters. Pushes white toward creatures; every creature-heavy white deck wants one.
Caretaker's Talent: Solid GW/token build-around, not a bomb. The draw-on-token-ETB engine is real card advantage in Rabbits/go-wide, and level 2's token-copy plus level 3's anthem give a top end. B- grade and 58.3% GIH WR are honest; take it as a strong role-player that gets better the more tokens you make.
Carrot Cake: Top-tier white common — LR publicly recanted their soft review to call it the best common in the set. A 2-mana Food that makes two 1/1 Rabbits and scries twice (ETB + sac) plus lifegain: it feeds GW Rabbits go-wide, WB Bats lifegain triggers, and any Food deck. 58.3% GIH at a 4.3 ALSA is a lock — take it.
Crumb and Get It: Solid combat trick, not a priority. One mana for +2/+2, and the gifted Food lets you tack on indestructible to blow out a block or push damage. The 55.7% GIH WR is respectable-average for a trick; a fine 20-25th-pick playable in any white deck, better in aggressive GW/RW.
Dawn's Truce: Sideboard/trap. A protection trick that answers nothing and does nothing to the board — the negative IWD (-2.2) and sub-49% GIH confirm it's a dead card in most games; the 27% play rate means most drafters correctly leave it out. Only shines as a blowout vs board wipes.
Dewdrop Cure: Filler reanimation for go-wide/token shells that want cheap bodies back — Rabbits (GW) or graveyard decks. The gift downside and 2-MV cap make it low-impact; 50.4% GIH, negative IWD and 28% play confirm it's a fringe playable, not a maindeck lock.
Driftgloom Coyote: Solid premium — white's best common-tier removal-on-a-body. A 3/4 for 3WW that exiles an opposing creature while it lives, often growing to 4/5 when it hits something small. 57% GIH, 86% play rate, ALSA 3 all agree it's a first-few-picks white staple; just remember it gives the creature back if it dies.
Essence Channeler: Premium WB Bats build-around that snowballs fast: every lifegain trigger grows it, and the flying/vigilance turn-on and death-transfer of counters make it hard to answer profitably. Strong +4.5 IWD on a two-drop; jam it in any lifegain shell and it's a solid pick even outside Bats.
Feather of Flight: Premium common-quality aura that dodges the usual card-disadvantage trap: it cantrips, so it's card-neutral, and flash + flying turns any body into an evasive threat or combat trick. 72.9% play rate and 57.1% GIH — take it early, snap it into any white deck.
Flowerfoot Swordmaster: One-drop Mice enabler with Offspring flexibility and a Valiant team-pump, but flat -0.3 IWD and middling 54.5% GIH WR say it's a curve-filler, not a payoff. Fine early body in RW/GW go-wide; don't overvalue the B grade — it needs the aggressive shell to shine.
Harvestrite Host: Premium GW Rabbits uncommon and a solid body anywhere. A 3/3 for three that pumps and, on the second Rabbit ETB each turn, draws — trivial to hit in a go-wide Rabbit shell. 59% GIH with +3.2 IWD and a 3.4 ALSA confirms it's a real payoff, not filler.
Hop to It: Premium GW Rabbits build-around glue. Three bodies for three mana is the format's best go-wide payoff — feeds Offspring/anthem synergies and posts the highest white common GIH WR (58.8%) with a huge +3.5 IWD. First-pick-worthy in Rabbits, a solid include anywhere white goes wide.
Intrepid Rabbit: The best white common per LoL's retro (edging Carrot Cake) — a 3/2 for 2W that almost always pays Offspring 1 to leave two bodies plus a pump. +2.6 IWD and 57.9% GIH make it a premium go-wide engine in GW Rabbits and a fine curve-filler in any white deck.
Jackdaw Savior: Premium WU Birds payoff and a fine 3/1 flyer anywhere — every flyer death recurs a smaller creature, snowballing evasive value. LR calls it good in every white deck; 56.5% GIH at a 2.2 ALSA backs a high pick, best in the flyers lane.
Jolly Gerbils: Good role-player in gift/Food decks. A 2/3 for 1W that draws whenever you give a gift — real value, but LR notes you never want three and it competes with better gift payoffs. Above-average 55% GIH; take it as a solid early pick in decks with multiple gift cards, filler otherwise.
Lifecreed Duo: A flying enabler for WB/GW go-wide lifegain — each other creature ETB drips a life, feeding Starscape Cleric and Bats drain. Middling 55.5% and low +1.7 IWD mark it as a role-player, not a payoff: fine early curve flyer that only shines with a critical mass of tokens.
Mabel's Mettle: Fine combat trick, nothing more — the negative IWD (-1.1) flags a card that's dead in your opener and only shines when drawn into a board. Double-pump is real blowout potential in go-wide GW/RW, but it's a role-player, not a priority.
Mouse Trapper: Flash 3/2 that taps a blocker when you target it — a tempo trick on a body, but the negative -2.7 IWD and 51.8% GIH WR mark it as a below-average filler outside a dedicated Valiant deck. C card; playable in RW Mice, cuttable elsewhere.
Nettle Guard: Filler-to-role-player white common. A 3/1 for two that survives combat when you target it (Valiant), with a sac-for-artifact/enchantment mode as built-in sideboard tech. Aggressive stat but flimsy: 54.6% GIH and a negative IWD say it's an early-curve body for RW Mice, not a card you prioritize.
Parting Gust: Flexible white removal at instant speed. Gift the Fish for a clean exile, or keep it to blink your own ETB back with a counter — versatility that plays both offense and defense. 53.7% GIH is modest for removal but the double-white and temporary-exile drawback explain it; a fine role-player, not a bomb.
Pileated Provisioner: Filler flyer. A 3/4 flyer for five with a small counter is a fine roleplayer at the top of a curve but nothing to prioritize — flat +0.2 IWD and a 6.2 ALSA say it wheels; take it late to round out a deck short on evasion.
Rabbit Response: A false-friend combat trick — the +2/+1 team pump plus scry looks splashy but LR flags it as "the response you don't need." Four mana double-white is stiff and the -0.7 IWD shows it underdelivers. Playable in aggressive GW/RW go-wide, not an auto-include.
Repel Calamity: Premium white removal — cheap instant-speed kill for anything the format cares about (4+ power/toughness catches most beaters and bombs). 57% GIH and 83% play rate confirm it clears the top of curves reliably; the only whiff is small utility creatures, so it's an early pick but not quite unconditional.
Salvation Swan: Top-tier WU Birds rare and a flash flying 3/3 that's fine anywhere. The blink saves a creature from removal, re-triggers ETBs, and grants evasion; A- grade plus a very early 2.0 ALSA back it. GD_WR (58.3%) beating OH shows it's best drawn as a reactive tool.
Season of the Burrow: White bomb — 61.7% GIH, +8.4 IWD, ALSA 1.5 means it's a first-pick every time. Five petals of flexible tokens/exile-removal/reanimation scales from turn 5 into an unbeatable late game. Slam it; the modality means it's never dead.
Seasoned Warrenguard: One-drop that swings as a 3/2 whenever you have a token — cheap aggression for GW Rabbits. The 57.1% GIH WR and strong 60.3% OH WR flatter it because it's best on curve in a go-wide start; the C grade is closer to the truth as a synergy-gated role-player.
Shrike Force: Solid WU Birds/white uncommon — a 1/3 flyer with double strike and vigilance that turns any pump or +1/+1 counter into a huge evasive clock. Needs help to threaten but blocks and attacks freely. 55.5% GIH and 3.7 ALSA make it a reliable playable, not a bomb.
Sonar Strike: Better than it looks — LR's format-riser. Four damage to any attacking/blocking/tapped creature at instant speed is real removal, and the 3 life is gravy in WB Bats. The C+ grade undersells it; 55.8% GIH confirms it overperforms. Prioritize as your removal in Bats, playable anywhere white.
Star Charter: Solid WB Bats roleplayer. A 3/1 flyer that reliably digs for cheap creatures once your lifegain/loss triggers are online — the card-advantage engine buys the attrition game BLB rewards. 54.1% GIH and a strong B grade; better than it looks, but the 3/1 body dies to everything.
Starfall Invocation: White sweeper bomb — a Wrath that can gift-recur your best creature back to your side, swinging a stalled board hard. This medium-slow format rewards board wipes; 57.0% GIH, 2.1 ALSA and A+ grade make it a slam wherever you're white.
Thistledown Players: Filler. A vanilla 3/3 for 2W whose attack trigger untaps a permanent — cute for pseudo-vigilance or mana untaps but rarely relevant. Negative IWD and sub-50 play rate say it's a curve body you cut when your white deck has options; only marginally better in combo-y untap builds.
Valley Questcaller: Bomb-tier GW/RW anthem — this is the card the format's go-wide decks are built around. 64.1% GIH, a monstrous +10.4 IWD, and 1.6 ALSA are elite; the team pump plus scry-on-entry makes a wide board lethal fast. First-pick it and lean into Rabbits/Mice/Bats/Birds.
Warren Elder: Filler two-drop that curves fine and offers a late-game mana sink for go-wide GW Rabbits. The flat IWD (-0.1) confirms it's a body first — 55.5% GIH is archetype lift from playing it in the right token deck, not raw power. Playable, unexciting.
Warren Warleader: Rabbit bomb and go-wide engine — a 4/4 for four with Offspring that either makes a tapped attacker or anthems your team every combat. Elite numbers across the board (63.2% GIH WR, +9.9 IWD, ALSA 1.4) confirm the A grade. First-pick that snowballs any board; slam it.
Wax-Wane Witness: Mid WB Bats role-player. A 2/4 flyer with vigilance for four that swings bigger whenever you gain or lose life on your turn — fine in a lifegain-drain shell, mediocre elsewhere. 54.1% GIH but only 49% play rate: a synergy body that's replaceable when Bats isn't your deck.
Whiskervale Forerunner: Strong RW Valiant engine and a fine standalone 3/4. Any spell or ability targeting it digs five deep and cheats a 3-drop into play on your turn — a snowball once you have tricks to trigger it. ALSA 2.0 and B+ grade mark it a high pick; the 56% GIH is Valiant-conditional but reliably good.
Azure Beastbinder: Premium UB Rats rare and a near-bomb — the +8.6 IWD and 60% OH_WR are elite. An evasive 1/3 that neutralizes their best creature every attack (strips abilities, shrinks to 2/2), acting as repeatable pseudo-removal plus a clock. First-pick it; it wins games nearly single-handed.
Bellowing Crier: Filler 2/1 loot for GU Frogs — the ETB draw-discard smooths draws and feeds graveyard/discard payoffs but the body dies to everything. 53.4% GIH and 47% play mark it as a replaceable role-player, best when you have discard synergies to fuel.
Calamitous Tide: Niche tempo-value spell for GU Frogs / control. Six mana to bounce two and loot two is slow, but the +4.9 IWD and 58% drawn-WR show it swings games it lands in — the low OH WR flags it as a late-game card you don't want early. A fine top-end for grindy blue decks, not a slam.
Daring Waverider: Value finisher for UR/spells decks: a 4/4 that flashbacks your best cheap instant/sorcery from the yard, effectively a two-for-one. LoL notes it fell flat because green was pushed, but it's still useful in UR. GD_WR 59.9% vs OH 52.6% marks it a grindy late-game card, not a tempo play.
Dazzling Denial: Cheap conditional counter — a WU Birds card that gets meaningfully better (pay-4 tax) with a Bird out. The +4.2 IWD and 55.3% GIH are strong for a reactive spell, but the low 45.7% play rate says it's niche; sideboard-flex in tempo Birds, not a maindeck staple elsewhere.
Dire Downdraft: The best mono-blue common per 17Lands despite the humble C grade — a {2}{U} instant against attackers/tapped that tucks a threat to the bottom for a huge tempo swing. +4.5 IWD and 56.6% GIH WR back the LR upgrade; premium interaction for any blue deck, take earlier than it looks.
Dour Port-Mage: Premium GU Frogs glue and the archetype's engine. A 1/3 for two that draws whenever your creatures blink/bounce and can bounce its own ETBs for {1}{U}. The +7.1 IWD and 2.8 ALSA are elite for a rare — it snowballs any blink deck. Take it high and build Frogs around it.
Eddymurk Crab: UR spells-payoff finisher with a huge draw-it swing (+6.0 IWD, 59.4% GD WR). Flash, a tap-two ETB, and a cost that plummets as your graveyard fills mean it lands as a tempo blowout in the late game. The 51.7% OH shows it's dead early — a build-around top-end, not a curve-filler.
Eluge, the Shoreless Sea: Build-around mono-blue-ish bomb, not a slam — triple-U and the Island payoff mean you need a heavy-blue base to unlock the cost reduction and growing body. In the right deck (44% play rate shows it's often not) the +6.4 IWD is real; provisional A in dedicated Ux tempo, filler otherwise.
Finch Formation: Down. A 2/2 flyer that grants temporary flying, with Offspring for scaling — LR says it "should be good but doesn't have a home often enough." 51.0% GIH and 27% play confirm marginal; only worth it in a dedicated WU Birds go-wide build.
Gossip's Talent: Trap / expert-only. The surveil-on-ETB base is weak and the level-2 unblockable wants a build you rarely have; D+ grade and 49% GIH confirm it's overdrafted. LR: good in the right deck, bad where it's forced — you have to know. Pass unless you're deep UB/UR go-wide with evasion payoffs.
Into the Flood Maw: Cheap tempo bounce, best in UB where LoL flags it as a green-meta counter (bounce your creature in response to their fight). One mana to reset an ETB, save a creature, or push damage; the gift upgrade hits any nonland. Role-player interaction — draw-conditioned 58.2% GD_WR confirms it wants to be held.
Kitnap: Premium blue removal disguised as an aura — steal any creature and either stun-lock it three turns (no gift) or hand them a card. A- grade earned: 57.5% GIH, ALSA 2.8. The gift-vs-stun split adds flexibility; take it highly in any blue deck.
Kitsa, Otterball Elite: Strong UR spells payoff — a 1/3 with vigilance, prowess, built-in looting, and spell-copy once she hits power 3. +7.4 IWD and 79% play rate show she pulls her weight even outside a pure Otters deck. B is right; a high pick in spells-matter, a fine two-drop elsewhere.
Knightfisher: Niche WU Birds payoff. A 4/5 flyer for five is a fine body, and each nontoken Bird spits out a Fish token, but at {3}{U}{U} it's clunky and only 48% play rate. 54.7% GIH with strong +4.7 IWD says it's good when Birds is open, mediocre as a generic five-drop.
Lightshell Duo: LoL's 'clunky over-performer' award — a 3/4 for 3U that surveils 2 and carries prowess. Goes very late (ALSA 7.0, 38.9% play) yet posts 55.6% GIH with +4.5 IWD; one of blue's quietly best commons. Wheel it and jam in any blue deck, especially UR spells.
Long River Lurker: Strong GU Frogs body — a 2/3 with ward that grants the team ward, plus a repeatable unblockable-and-blink enabler to re-trigger your ETBs. +4.9 IWD and 57% GIH; a premium uncommon in Frogs that protects your value engine and sneaks damage. High pick when GU is open.
Long River's Pull: Conditional counter for UU decks — hard counter on creatures, upgradable to anything via gift. The +5.1 IWD is inflated by control games; 54.7% GIH but only 38% play. A fine reactive tool for grindy blue decks, unexciting elsewhere.
Mind Spiral: Niche payoff card-draw. Five mana for three cards (plus a stun if you gift a Fish token) is powerful but clunky; LSV loved casting it but got pushed out by Frogs. High drawn-WR (56%) yet low OH and 28% play rate mark it a late-game control finisher — playable in slow blue decks, cuttable in most.
Mindwhisker: Underrated UB Rats/Threshold payoff — LR revised it up to one of the best payoffs, brutal in multiples. Upkeep surveil fuels its own Threshold, and a team-wide -1/-0 warps combat once online. GD_WR 59.0% over OH 54.4% shows it's a build-around that rewards a graveyard-focused deck.
Mockingbird: Powerful blue rare — a flying X-cost clone of your best creature (or theirs), scaling with the game. LoL notes Ben would splash it over playable golds. The oh_wr/gd_wr gap (53→58.8) shows it's a mid-game value engine, not a turn-2 play; premium pick.
Nightwhorl Hermit: Threshold sleeper that stays a vanilla 1/4 wall until you have seven cards in the graveyard, then turns unblockable. 16.6% play rate and D grade say it rarely got there; 50.2% GIH WR is replacement-level. Deep UB Threshold only, and even there it's a late-pick filler.
Otterball Antics: UR Otters/spells role-player. Makes a prowess Otter and, via flashback, a bigger counter'd one — two bodies plus two prowess triggers across the game. The GD/OH split (55.8% vs 51.1%) marks it as a synergy card that overperforms when drawn into an Otters engine, not a slam.
Pearl of Wisdom: Efficient card draw, best in Otters where it's a two-mana Divination. Even at three it refuels well — +5.8 IWD and 57.8% drawn WR reward the card advantage this slow format prizes. Low play rate (39%) reflects it being a control/UR pick, not universal; solid in the right lane.
Plumecreed Escort: Premium WU Birds uncommon and a great tempo/protection play — a 2-mana flash flyer that ambushes attackers and shields your key creature from removal at instant speed. +4.4 IWD, 56.3% GIH; the flash flyer that overperforms and slots into any blue deck, not just Birds.
Portent of Calamity: The A- grade is a trap — LR grades it F ("5 mana to draw two cards, now I must quit"). It whiffs on type-diversity and rarely hits the free-spell threshold. 52.8% GIH and a dismal 19.8% play settle it: a fringe card, not a rare payoff.
Run Away Together: Marginal tempo. Bouncing one of yours and one of theirs rarely profits when you're the synergy deck trying to build a board — LR downgraded it to 'very medium, gets booted most of the time.' The +2.2 IWD is deceptive; 40% play rate is the truth. Sideboard/flex, not a maindeck lock.
Season of Weaving: Premium blue mana sink and a flexible bomb — draw, copy your best permanent, or Evacuation the board, scaling with your mana. 60.7% GIH and +9.7 IWD on a mythic that's always live; the bounce mode alone swings stalled games. High pick in any blue deck.
Shore Up: One-mana protection-plus-untap trick that also enables a surprise block or pushes damage. The oh/gd split (50.7 vs 56.4) marks it as a drawn card, not an opener — a role-player that saves your bomb from removal. Fine in tempo/aura blue, filler elsewhere.
Shoreline Looter: Consistent blue value engine — an unblockable 1/1 for {1}{U} that loots or straight-up draws once you hit Threshold, and wears Builder's Talent counters beautifully. +8.2 IWD and 60.4% GIH WR outrun the B- grade. Prioritize in UB/UR; the evasion makes the card-filtering reliable.
Skyskipper Duo: Filler blue common. A 3/3 flyer for five that blinks one of your creatures for an ETB re-trigger — real GU Frogs synergy but overcosted and slow. The big OH/GD gap (50.3% vs 56.1%) and 6.8 ALSA say it's a late-table body that's only good with ETBs to abuse.
Spellgyre: Flexible blue two-of: hard counter or surveil-2-draw-2 at instant speed. The modality makes it never dead and the card-advantage half suits BLB's grind (57.6% GD WR, +4.9 IWD). The 52.8% OH shows it wants to be drawn, not in your opener; a good role-player in UR/UB tempo-control.
Splash Lasher: Solid blue uncommon — a 3/3 for four that taps-and-stuns a blocker/attacker (soft removal) and offers Offspring to double the body and the stun. +5.4 IWD and 59.7% GD_WR make it a reliable tempo/value piece; a comfortable early-mid pick in any blue deck.
Splash Portal: Cheap one-mana blink that re-triggers an ETB and cantrips off a Bird/Frog/Otter/Rat — a GU Frogs enabler par excellence. 55.2% GIH and 55% play show it earns its slot when built around ETBs; mediocre as a pure combat trick.
Stormchaser's Talent: Premium build-around and one of the best Talents. A one-mana Otter token that scales into a spell recursion and token engine for UR Otters, but the ETB body alone justifies the pick anywhere. 58.8% GIH, +7.4 IWD, ALSA 3.4 — jam it early; it's a rare that overdelivers and anchors the spells archetype.
Sugar Coat: Solid blue removal disguised as an aura — flash it to strip a creature down to a harmless Food, answering bombs at instant speed. Not a clean kill (they can sac for life), but the only real removal blue offers. C+ undersells it; GD_WR 56.6% marks a reactive role-player worth maindecking.
Thought Shucker: Late-game filler — a 1/3 wall that only comes alive at seven graveyard cards, deep into a UB Rats/Threshold game. The 23.7% play rate and 48.5% OH WR confirm it's a low-priority body most decks cut; playable only in dedicated mill/threshold shells.
Thundertrap Trainer: Blue two-drop that digs four deep for a noncommittal noncreature/land hit, with late-game Offspring reach. +6.1 IWD and 57.7% GIH WR reward the card selection in spells decks. Solid B-range role-player; better in UR/spells shells than as a generic filler.
Valley Floodcaller: UR Otters build-around rare and a spells-tempo engine. Flash, lets you cast noncreature spells at flash speed, and pumps + untaps your Birds/Frogs/Otters/Rats on every noncment spell — a pseudo-Vengevine-style attack step. 55.1% GIH understates it; the 2.9 ALSA and +4.2 IWD show it's a ceiling card that demands a spell-dense deck.
Waterspout Warden: Marginal GU Frogs filler. A 3/2 for 2U that flies only when you've made a token that turn — a real hoop this format doesn't always clear. 52.2% GIH and ALSA 7.5 mark it a 22nd+ pick; a body that occasionally connects, nothing to prioritize.
Wishing Well: Trap. LR grades it F — too slow and setup-heavy, needing multiple turns of coin counters plus spells in the yard before it does anything. The 56.6% GIH is a mirage from the tiny 10% play rate (only skilled durdle decks ran it); the 50.2% OH_WR and D+ grade are the truth. Skip.
Agate-Blade Assassin: Solid BR/aggro two-drop — a 1/3 that drains and gains a life on every attack, chipping the clock while stabilizing. The higher OH_WR (56.0) vs drawn shows it wants to come down early; 65.8% play, a dependable role-player in aggressive black decks.
Bandit's Talent: Role-player build-around for UB discard. The ETB discard is real disruption and levels punish an empty hand, but it needs a dedicated discard shell to shine — average 52.6% GIH reflects that it's often played without support. Solid in committed UB Rats, mediocre goodstuff filler otherwise.
Bonebind Orator: Filler-plus BG Squirrels body: a vanilla 2/2 up front that becomes graveyard recursion late by exiling itself to rebuy a creature. +0.2 IWD says the value is marginal and slow; a fine curve-filler in grindy Squirrels decks but never a priority pick.
Bonecache Overseer: One-drop card-advantage engine for BG Forage/Food — the OH WR (57.7%) actually beats drawn, unusual, meaning it wants to be cast early to start looting. Solid synergy piece in Squirrels/sacrifice decks; mediocre outside them. Good role-player when the graveyard/Food theme is online.
Coiling Rebirth: Reanimation payoff at {3}{B}{B} that returns a creature and, if you gift, clones it — huge with a bomb in the yard. The 53.6% GIH WR and weak 49.7% OH WR show it's dead early and shines drawn (56.0% GD WR). B grade is generous; a fine BG grind top-end, not a first-pick.
Consumed by Greed: Premium black removal-ish uncommon. An edict that forces the sacrifice of their biggest creature, and with the gift you rebuy a creature from your yard for tempo-neutral value. 58.8% GIH, 88.7% play rate — reliable interaction that dodges hexproof/big bodies. Take it high in any black deck.
Cruelclaw's Heist: Double-black Thoughtseize-plus that steals and lets you cast the card — but it's a two-for-one that does nothing to the board. LR panned it (D, 'too slow') and 53.2% GIH agrees; the BB cost and sorcery speed drag it down. A situational pick, sideboard-y against combo/bombs.
Daggerfang Duo: Solid black common, third-best Duo per LoL — a 3/2 deathtouch that trades up all day and mills 2 to feed UB Threshold. 55.5% GIH; a fine early body anywhere and genuinely good in blue-black. Slightly underrated early in the format; take it as a reliable roleplayer.
Darkstar Augur: Ignore the C- grade — live data (60.4% GIH, +6.4 IWD, 2.1 ALSA) makes this a top-tier WB Bats engine. A 3-mana 2/3 flyer that draws every turn, and terrifying with Offspring {B} for a token. Numot/LR agree: don't run without the Offspring option, but jam it high.
Diresight: Role-player card advantage. Surveil 2 then draw 2 for 2B is efficient refuel that also feeds graveyard/Forage synergies, but the 2 life and sorcery speed keep it a support card, not a bomb. 54.5% GIH with a low 36% play rate — a fine glue card for BG grind decks, not a high pick.
Downwind Ambusher: Sleeper-turned-excellent BR/BG uncommon — both LoL and LR revised it UP after the -1/-1 mode. Flash 4/2 that ambushes an attacker or finishes a damaged creature means every combat against you goes badly; 59.6% GIH and 87% play back the upgrade. Strong pick, treat as removal-on-a-body.
Early Winter: Overcosted catch-all removal at five mana, but it exiles anything and hits enchantments in a bind. The negative-leaning stats (50.6% OH, ALSA 5.8) say it's slow filler removal — playable when black is light on answers, but you'd rather have Savor or Nocturnal Hunger.
Feed the Cycle: Top black common by win rate — unconditional {1}{B} kill on creatures/planeswalkers, cheapened by forage or {B}. 90% play rate and +4.9 IWD confirm the B+ read; premium removal that BG/Food especially fuels for free. Take it very highly in any black deck.
Fell: Premium black removal — unconditional destroy for {1}{B} at sorcery speed, the cleanest removal in a format where removal is scarce. 59.5% GIH, +5.9 IWD, 2.3 ALSA: this is a top-of-pack pick and the reason to be in black. Grade it up over the B.
Glidedive Duo: The universal black playable — 'goes in every black deck' (LoL). A 3/3 flyer that drains 2 and gains 2 on ETB does everything WB Bats wants: evasion, reach, lifegain trigger. 56.6% GIH and 74.7% play confirm the workhorse. Solid mid-pick, higher in Bats.
Hazel's Nocturne: Solid WB/black value instant — regrows up to two creatures from the yard while draining 2, a huge two-for-one that swings attrition games and turns on lifegain triggers. +2.5 IWD, 56.4% GIH belie the modest C grade; a strong mid-pick in grindy black decks.
Huskburster Swarm: Playable finisher for BG graveyard/Forage decks that fills the yard — cost-reduces toward a castable 6/6 menace deathtouch that trades up and closes. 53.7% GIH, 65.8% play; a fine top-end curve-topper when you're exiling/milling creatures, filler otherwise.
Iridescent Vinelasher: Strong early pick and BG/black beater. A one-mana 1/2 that pings the opponent every landfall, and Offspring doubles the triggers into a real clock. ALSA 2.1, 58% GIH and 85% play rate confirm it's a reliable value engine; take it highly in any black deck that can flood lands.
Maha, Its Feathers Night: Format bomb — a 6/5 flying trample for five that gives every opposing creature base toughness 1, so your whole team punches through and their blockers evaporate. Ward-discard protects it. 63.4% GIH, 1.3 ALSA, +9.9 IWD: first-pick, splash if you must.
Moonstone Harbinger: Strong WB Bats uncommon — a 1/3 flyer with deathtouch that trades up immediately, and its lifegain trigger snowballs your Bat team's power. 73.7% play rate, +3.1 IWD. Great in the drain deck; still a fine evasive deathtoucher anywhere black flies.
Nocturnal Hunger: Premium black common removal — unconditional destroy at instant speed, with a small Food/life cost. 90% play rate and near-universal expert praise (Numot: always want one, ideally more) beat the tepid LR C+. Prioritize highly; every black deck wants multiples.
Osteomancer Adept: Premium BG Squirrels/graveyard rare (LR's A-). A 2/2 deathtouch for two that trades up immediately, then becomes a recursion engine, recasting creatures from your yard by foraging. 59% GIH with a 2.1 ALSA — great even as a vanilla deathtoucher, busted in Forage decks. Early pick.
Persistent Marshstalker: UB Rats aggro two-drop that scales with your board and recurs off Threshold once your graveyard hits seven. A 3/1 that grows is fine early, and the recursion adds late-game reach. 56% GIH is good for a two-drop; a solid Rats pick, mediocre outside the tribe.
Psychic Whorl: Sideboard/filler. Sorcery-speed discard-two is low-impact in a creature format, and the surveil rider needs a Rat — outside dedicated UB Rats it's near-unplayable, hence the 13% play rate and D+. The +3.0 IWD is small-sample noise from the few Rats decks; leave it in the board.
Ravine Raider: Aggressive one-drop menace with a mana sink, at home in BR Lizards go-wide. Higher OH_WR (57.4) rewards curving it out turn one; 55.3% GIH but flat IWD and 45% play mark it a replaceable early beater, not a priority.
Rottenmouth Viper: Bomb. A 6/6 for 5B that sacrifices permanents to cheapen itself and repeatedly forces opponents to bleed 4, sac, or discard on every ETB and attack. ALSA 1.4, 92% play rate, LR grades it A — a first-pick finisher that ends grindy games single-handedly; take it over almost anything.
Ruthless Negotiation: Niche B disruption — a one-mana Duress-style exile with flashback for card advantage from the yard. 58% GIH but a low 55% play rate and C- grade say it's a sideboard/role-player: fine against bombs and control, weak against a flooded aggro board where there's nothing to strip.
Savor: Best black common removal, per LR/Numot/LoL consensus — instant-speed -2/-2 kills most of the curve AND makes Food for Forage/lifegain synergies. 89.2% play rate, 59.3% GIH. Premium: prioritize it in any black deck, especially BG and Builder's Talent shells.
Scales of Shale: Underrated instant that hands a creature +2/+0, lifelink, and indestructible — a two-for-one combat blowout plus a life swing, cheaper in Lizards. LR would take it over Savor in RB Lizards. 57.7% GIH WR and +3.2 IWD beat the C- grade; strong one-of in any black deck. UP.
Scavenger's Talent: BG Squirrels build-around — the doctrine's 'jam a Talent' rule applies. Level 1 turns creature deaths into Food, then it mills and reanimates. The C- grade badly undersells it: 56.3% GIH with a big OH/GD gap (53% vs 58.5%) is exactly the profile of a synergy engine that snowballs when you commit. Prioritize in BG.
Season of Loss: The best card in the set (LR A+). A modal wrath/draw/drain for 3BB that's an unbeatable swing at any board state — sac everyone, refill your hand, then drain them out. 65.7% GIH, +13.4 IWD, ALSA 1.6: a slam first-pick bomb, take it over anything.
Sinister Monolith: Filler value artifact — a slow drain-1-per-turn that sacs for two cards. Does nothing for the board and the -1.1 IWD plus sub-52% GIH show it's below replacement; the 51.8% play rate is generous. Only a late fill for grindy WB drain decks; usually cut.
Stargaze: Scalable card draw at a life cost — best in shells that offset the loss (WB/BG Food and lifegain), per LoL, and risky in BR which lacks mitigation. 54.5% GIH, 37% play; a solid role-player when your deck buys life, a liability when it doesn't.
Starlit Soothsayer: Role-player in WB Bats. A 2/2 flyer for 2B that surveils when you gain/lose life — evasion plus incidental graveyard filling, but the body is small and the trigger passive. Below-average 51.6% GIH; a fine curve flyer in lifegain-heavy Bat decks, cuttable filler elsewhere.
Starscape Cleric: Core WB Bats drain payoff — a can't-block 2/1 flyer that turns every lifegain trigger into reach, and Offspring lets it go wide to multiply the drain. LR's B undersells it in dedicated Bats; the lifegain engine of that archetype makes this a high pick, mediocre outside it.
Thornplate Intimidator: Playable BR/black aggro four-drop with real reach — the ETB drains 3 or strips a resource, and Offspring lets it go wide late. Middling stats (48.5% play, 52.4% OH) mark it as a solid role-player, not a bomb; better in the aggressive Lizards/sacrifice decks.
Thought-Stalker Warlock: "The LeBron James of Bloomburrow" — a 2/2 menace for {2}{B} whose ETB is targeted discard (best card if they lost life). 60.8% GIH WR, 89.6% play rate, B+ grade; an evasive body plus disruption that overdelivered all format. High pick in any black deck. UP.
Valley Rotcaller: Premium WB Bats/BG payoff — a 1/3 menace for two that drains for each other Squirrel, Bat, Lizard, or Rat you control, closing games fast in a go-wide deck. 58.6% GIH, +5.1 IWD, 2.0 ALSA: an early pick that scales with your tribe and gains you life to boot.
Wick, the Whorled Mind: Rat-tribal engine that snowballs a Snail into a Grixis-activated damage/draw finisher. Even without the {U}{B}{R} activation it's a 2/4 that builds a growing board in UB Rats. B+ grade and +4.4 IWD; 54.9% GIH is tribe-conditional. A strong Rats pick, filler elsewhere.
Wick's Patrol: Bomb-adjacent black uncommon — a 5/3 for six that mills 3 and hands you a scaling -X/-X, usually enough to two-for-one by killing something big on arrival. +6.3 IWD, 60.3% GIH and a B+ grade; premium removal-on-a-body that any black deck wants highly.
Agate Assault: Solid BR removal — four damage that exiles kills most of the format at sorcery speed, with artifact-hate flexibility. 54.3% GIH and 78.6% play make it a reliable maindeck kill spell; not premium (sorcery-speed) but always welcome in red.
Alania's Pathmaker: Solid aggressive role-player — the best Otter common. A 4/2 for 4 that impulse-draws a card, giving UR/RW spells decks a body plus fuel. Flat IWD and 54% GIH mark it good-not-great; a reliable midrange playable that curves and refuels, but don't prioritize it over real payoffs.
Artist's Talent: Trap — the worst Talent by far and essentially unplayable in Limited, as LR's F confirms. It does nothing on its own, needs a heavy noncreature-spell density BLB doesn't support, and the damage payoff rarely comes online. 46% GIH and 18.5% play rate; leave it in the pack.
Blacksmith's Talent: Underrated equipment Talent (LR bumped it up) — the Sword token makes it a real card immediately, and level 3's double-strike/haste closes games; combos with Starforged Sword. Best in RG/RW aggro or as a Builder's Talent splash piece. Flat IWD says it's a build-around, not a slam.
Blooming Blast: Flexible red burn — 2 damage to a creature, or gift a Treasure to also throw 3 to the face. The reach and Treasure-fixing give it range, but flat +0.8 IWD and 54.1% GIH WR make it a solid-not-premium removal spell. C+/B; fine in any red deck, take after the better kill.
Brambleguard Captain: Filler RW/red Mice role-player. A 2/3 for four that funnels its own power into one attacker each combat — fine in go-wide Mice but slow and small. Negative IWD and 53.9% GIH say it's a replaceable body; play it when you need the curve filler, not a priority.
Brazen Collector: Aggressive RG/Raccoon two-drop with a ritual kicker. First strike makes the 2/1 punch above its weight and the attack-mana ramps into expend payoffs. Note the split: 57.9% OH vs 52.2% GD — great early, dead late. Curve-filler for aggressive red, prioritize modestly.
Byway Barterer: Premium RG Raccoons rare and a great goodstuff body — a 3/3 menace for three that, on any turn you Expend 4, loots your hand into two fresh cards. Low 2.6 ALSA means it's taken early; +3.0 IWD, LR's B+. A clock plus card advantage; high pick in any red deck.
Coruscation Mage: Strong UR Otters/spells payoff — a 1R 2/2 (Offspring for a second) that pings each opponent on every noncreature spell, feeding "lost life" triggers without combat. LoL loves it in RB spells/control; 54.4% GIH, 71% play, a high pick in the spells lane.
Conduct Electricity: Filler removal — red's 'necessary evil.' Five mana to deal 6 is expensive and sorcery-speed-clunky at instant, but red is desperate for kill spells so it makes decks. LR's D+ and 52.5% GIH say it's a last-resort answer; run it when your BR/RG deck lacks better removal, cut it when it doesn't.
Emberheart Challenger: Premium RW Mice/UR aggro two-drop — haste, prowess, and Valiant card-advantage when you target it make it a snowballing threat that refills your hand. LR's B+ is right; 58.1% GIH with early 2.3 ALSA. High pick for any aggressive red deck built to target its own creatures.
Festival of Embers: Trap — a five-mana graveyard-recursion engine that does nothing the turn it lands and demands a spell-dense deck that BLB rarely supports. 48.1% GIH, 6.6% play rate is a near-unplayable verdict; the D+ grade is correct. Leave it in the pack.
Flamecache Gecko: Aggressive BR two-drop — a 2/2 that ramps into {B}{R} if you've dealt damage, plus a rummage outlet. The ritual and card-filtering suit Lizards/aggro, but flat +0.8 IWD and 56.3% GIH WR peg it as a solid role-player, not a payoff. Fine B- body in RB.
Dragonhawk, Fate's Tempest: Red bomb, mythic — a 5/5 flyer for five that immediately closes games. With even one other big creature it exiles cards for card advantage AND burns each opponent for 2 per card left. 62.3% GIH and +10.1 IWD with a 1.5 ALSA — a first-pick that wins on its own. LR's A over the B is correct.
Frilled Sparkshooter: Below-rate BR Lizards filler. Menace + reach on a 3/3 (or 4/4 if an opponent already bled) is fine on paper, but 3R is steep and the -2.0 IWD plus ALSA 6.7 mark it a late, replaceable body. Playable in a curve-hungry Lizards deck, otherwise cut.
Harnesser of Storms: Down — a disappointing spells-matter rare per LR (must play the exiled card THIS turn, doesn't line up with your best spells). The 1/4 body is defensive but the engine is clunky; -0.9 IWD, sub-51% GIH and 38% play rate confirm it underdelivers. Fringe UR playable at best.
Heartfire Hero: RW Mice all-star one-drop — Valiant grows it off your combat tricks and it deals a parting blast on death. The 60.9 OH_WR vs 53.1 drawn screams turn-one aggression; LR grades it A-ish. Premium in Mice/Valiant, mediocre if drawn late.
Hearthborn Battler: Strong aggressive rare for BR/UR spells. A 2/3 haste for 2R that pings 2 whenever anyone casts their second spell each turn — reach damage that closes games in a spells-dense deck. ALSA 2.7 and 82% play rate; the 53.6% GIH looks modest because it needs spell density, so it's a premium in the right build.
Hired Claw: Premium BR Lizards one-drop — the massive OH_WR/GD_WR split (66.4% vs 55.0%) screams a curve-topping aggro card that must land early. Pings on Lizard attacks and grows itself once you're dealing damage. LR's A- is right in dedicated Lizards; jam it as a proactive 1-drop, weaker on the draw.
Hoarder's Overflow: Trap despite LoL's anecdote — the numbers are damning: 45.4% GIH, -6.4 IWD, 11.9% play rate. Discarding your hand to redraw is a nonbo with everything, and it's slow. LR's 'down' read wins. Sideboard curio for dedicated RB control only.
Kindlespark Duo: Pinger that untaps on every noncreature spell — a UR Otters engine in theory, but a 1/3 for {2}{R} with -2.0 IWD, 49.4% GIH WR, and 38.9% play rate is below replacement in practice. Niche spells-deck filler only; leave it in the pack elsewhere.
Manifold Mouse: RW Mice bomb-uncommon-tier rare and one of the best two-drops in the set. Offspring 2 gives two bodies, and it hands a Mouse double strike or trample every combat — that's lethal reach in go-wide aggro. 63.1% GIH, +10 IWD: near a first pick in Mice, take it very high.
Might of the Meek: Cantripping trample trick, best in RW Mice. One mana, replaces itself, and pushes evasive damage — the cantrip keeps it from being a blowout risk. Negative IWD (-1.0) shows it's a synergy card you want cast, not drawn late. Fine role-player in aggressive red, not a priority.
Playful Shove: Filler cantrip removal. One damage is thin in BLB, but stapling a card draw makes it a painless include that picks off X/1s and pings for reach. LR's D is harsh — the +0.7 IWD and 54% GIH say it's a fine late roleplayer, not a priority; take it to smooth a red deck.
Quaketusk Boar: Efficient beater — a 5/5 reach/trample/haste for five that blocks flyers, races, and immediately attacks. No synergy needed; 56.0% GIH and 80.7% play make it a dependable curve-topper for any RG/red midrange deck, solid but unspectacular.
Rabid Gnaw: Premium red removal — efficient fight-style. For 1R your creature pumps +1/+0 and fights, killing most things while your body usually survives. 58% GIH, +4.5 IWD, 85% play rate; the only cost is needing a creature in play, so it's an early pick in any red deck with a decent board.
Raccoon Rallier: Filler — a 2/2 whose sorcery-speed haste-granting rarely earns its card, reflected in a poor 51.4% GIH, -3.5 IWD, and 6.3 ALSA. Only relevant in a specific RG go-tall/Expend build wanting to rush a fatty; otherwise it's a replaceable body you cut for anything better.
Reptilian Recruiter: Situational BR/Lizards finisher — a 4/2 trample whose Threaten effect is unconditional with another Lizard out but otherwise only steals small creatures. Below-even IWD (-0.7) and 44.7% play rate flag it as a build-around, not a staple; good only in the tribal Lizard deck.
Roughshod Duo: Vanilla-ish 3/2 trample for {2}{R} with an Expend 4 pump — a generic RG body that wants the ramp-heavy Raccoon shell. Negative -1.7 IWD and 53.2% GIH WR mark it filler; the C grade is right. Curve-filler in aggressive red, easily cut.
Sazacap's Brew: Sideboard/filler red common. Discard-a-card, draw-two at instant speed with a small prowess/pump rider via the gift — card-neutral-to-negative and clunky. 50.8% GIH, negative IWD, 31.7% play rate: don't play it outside a spells deck desperate for card flow.
Season of the Bold: Modal red payoff — Treasure ramp, impulse draw, and a spell-slinger damage engine. B per LR but only 53.6% GIH; the C+ live read is more honest since it does nothing immediately and wants a built-around UR/BR shell. A good-not-great mid-pick, ceiling higher in spells decks.
Steampath Charger: Below-replacement red common — a 2/1 for two that pings 1 on death, with an expensive Offspring 2. The -2.8 IWD and 6.2 ALSA are damning; it's a weak aggro body that trades down. Only a filler two-drop in a BR/RW deck desperate for early plays; usually last picks.
Stormsplitter: A trap outside a dedicated UR spells deck — the 42.8% GIH and -7.6 IWD are damning, the worst on this list. A 1/4 that copies itself per spell needs a critical mass of instants/sorceries to do anything; a narrow build-around, near-unplayable elsewhere.
Sunspine Lynx: Overrated — take it down. A 5/4 for 2RR with lifegain-hate and nonbasic burn reads like a bomb but LR calls it 'a pile of stats with random extra that doesn't cut it,' downgrading it; negative IWD and 51% GIH confirm. A playable body in aggressive red, but not the high pick the B grade suggests.
Take Out the Trash: Best red common and premium removal — LoL calls it exactly that. Three damage at instant speed for two mana kills most of the format, and RG Raccoons even get loot value. 56.9% GIH understates it because it's often a maindeck lock; prioritize highly in any red deck.
Teapot Slinger: Solid RG/Raccoon Expend four-drop — a 3/4 menace that turns your natural mana-spending into repeatable reach. LR grades it B; 69.3% play, 53.6% GIH is fine. A dependable body-plus-upside role-player in Expend decks; unexciting but always makes the cut there.
Valley Flamecaller: Lord-ish rare that adds +1 to all damage from your Lizards/Mice/Otters/Raccoons — a burn/aggro multiplier that turns pingers and attackers lethal. 86% play rate, +3.1 IWD, B/B+; a strong aggro payoff in BR/RW/UR. Take it high when you're in a damage-based red deck.
War Squeak: Trap/sideboard red common. A 1-mana aura granting +1/+1, haste, and a can't-block that reads like an aggro finisher but is card disadvantage that gets blown out by removal. 48.9% GIH, -3.1 IWD, 18.7% play rate — one of the worst playables; leave it in the board.
Whiskerquill Scribe: Weak RW Valiant looter. A 2/2 that rummages when you target it is fragile and card-neutral, and the numbers are ugly — 51.8% GIH, -3.3 IWD, 45.8% play. Needs a Valiant-dense deck to justify the slot; mostly filler you'd rather not run.
Wildfire Howl: Situational UR/red sweeper — 2 damage to all creatures is the answer to GW Rabbits and other go-wide token decks, with a gift mode adding a targeted point. Narrow (32.7% play rate) but format-defining when you're the control deck; LoL calls it an important UR include. Sideboard-flexible C.
Bakersbane Duo: Premium green common — LoL rates it best-or-second-best in the set. A 1G 2/2 that makes Food on ETB and pumps on Expend 4, giving body, Food-synergy fuel, and combat reach. 89.7% play, 57.3% GIH; take it highly in any green deck (BG/RG).
Valley Rally: Filler combat trick. +2/+0 team pump (plus first strike if you gift a Food) can blow out a go-wide attack, but giving the opponent lifegain and the sorcery-like all-in nature make it swingy. Negative IWD and 37% play rate — a niche finisher for RW/GW go-wide, not a maindeck staple.
Bark-Knuckle Boxer: Solid RG/aggro two-drop — a 3/2 that becomes indestructible the turn you Expend 4, letting it attack into anything or survive combat tricks and blocks. 56.3% GIH is fine; a good aggressive body that rewards curving out, but the indestructible needs four-mana turns to matter.
Brambleguard Veteran: Good RG Raccoons/Expend uncommon — a 3/4 for three that anthems the team when you expend 4, which the Raccoon curve does naturally. B grade, 79.3% play, ALSA 3.9 confirm a reliable playable. Solid body first, payoff second; take it in the Expend deck.
Bushy Bodyguard: Excellent BG Squirrel two-drop — Offspring for a go-wide start plus a forage ETB that makes it a 4/3, doubling as forage fodder and Food synergy. B+ grade, 85% play rate, and +1.6 IWD understate its flexibility. Strong early pick in Squirrels/Food; combines with Cultivator.
Cache Grab: Breakout BG Squirrels/green Forage common — LR upgraded it to a top green common. A 2-mana instant that mills four, returns any permanent to hand, and makes Food with a Squirrel: card advantage plus graveyard fuel and Food for foraging. 57.7% GIH understates its role; prioritize it in BG.
Clifftop Lookout: GU/ramp value creature — a 1/2 reach body that ramps a land into play, fixing and accelerating toward your top end. Defensively fine and enables bombs, but the small body caps it (53.2% GIH). Solid role-player in ramp/Frogs, a 15th-ish pick where you want fixing.
Curious Forager: Solid BG Squirrels glue — a 3/2 that forages to regrow any permanent, an efficient value body that fuels and rewards the Forage engine. +1.0 IWD understates it; 55.6% GIH and 85% play rate show it's a comfortable mid pick and a staple two-for-one in green Forage decks.
Druid of the Spade: A 2/3 that becomes a 4/3 trampler whenever you control any token — reliable in GW Rabbits/token or Food shells. LR grades it B; 54.1% GIH and 50% play mark it a fine role-player that needs token support to hit above its weight.
Fecund Greenshell: Bomb — the best card in this chunk. A 4/6 reach for 3GG that ramps and card-advantages on every high-toughness creature ETB and anthems your team at 10 lands. 64% GIH and a monster +11.4 IWD; take it over nearly everything in any green deck, it wins the long game by itself.
For the Common Good: Trap in Limited — LR's D- nails it: an XX build-around demanding a wide token board you rarely have, and even then it's win-more. 45.6% GIH and a 12% play rate confirm it. The B grade is a pre-data mirage; skip it outside a dedicated token deck already winning.
Galewind Moose: Premium green fatty — flash + vigilance/reach/trample makes it a 6/6 ambush that blocks flyers, trades up, and never gets stranded. 90.6% play, +4.1 IWD, ALSA 2.8. A top-tier green common-slot pull; take it early in any green deck.
Hazardroot Herbalist: 1/4 attack-anthem that grants deathtouch to token targets — cute in GW go-wide but defensively statted and low-impact. Negative -2.4 IWD and 51.4% GIH WR say it underperformed; C+ is generous. Marginal role-player for token decks, cut when you have better.
Heaped Harvest: Role-player green common. A 3-mana Food that fetches a basic tapped on ETB and sac (mana fixing) while counting as Food for Forage payoffs. 52.7% GIH and +0.8 IWD are modest — it's a utility glue piece for BG/RG Food decks and splashes, not a card you actively want maindeck without the synergy.
High Stride: Cheap green combat trick with a defensive bent — +1/+3, reach, and untap for one mana, blowing out attacks or ambushing flyers. LR's B is generous; 54.4% GIH and 31.6% play mark it a situational sideboard-flex trick. Good against fliers, otherwise a fringe include.
Hivespine Wolverine: Premium green uncommon — a 5/4 for five with a flexible ETB (grow a creature, fight a token, or blow up an artifact/enchantment), so it's never a dead body. LR's A; +3.5 IWD, 57.6% GIH and 89% play rate. A hard-to-beat threat plus utility; take it highly in any green deck.
Honored Dreyleader: BG Squirrels payoff — enters scaling off Squirrels/Food and grows with each one, a trampling threat that snowballs in the right shell. 55.5% GIH, 67% play; a solid uncommon when your deck is heavy on Squirrels and Food, mediocre as a random body.
Hunter's Talent: Premium — the mythic-uncommon groan test. The ETB alone is a removal fight for 1G, then it snowballs into pump/trample and card draw; LR: 'slots into any green deck, asks nothing, and they got one of the best cards.' 61% GIH, ALSA 2.1 — near first-pick in green, upgrade over the B+ grade.
Innkeeper's Talent: Bomb build-around and one of the best commons-slot rares — LR's A/A+ ('the game was never a contest'). Free combat counters that scale into ward protection then counter-doubling; runs away with any board. 62.7% GIH, +10.1 IWD, 93% play rate. First-pick in green.
Keen-Eyed Curator: Sneaky-strong green rare — a two-mana 3/3 that grows into a 7/7 trampler while hosing both Threshold and Forage graveyards. LoL calls it 'more oppressive than it appears.' 58.9% GIH, +5.5 IWD, ALSA 2.0. Premium two-drop; prioritize it, especially against BG.
Longstalk Brawl: Efficient green removal — a one-mana fight spell, better with a +1/+1 counter if you gift a token (which also feeds your opponent). 87.5% play rate and +1.8 IWD; the C+ grade undersells how much cheap green interaction matters in a removal-light format. Solid playable, take it.
Lumra, Bellow of the Woods: Green bomb, mythic — a */* for six equal to your lands, with vigilance and reach, that mills four and returns ALL milled lands to the battlefield, ramping and growing itself huge. 59.8% GIH with +7.6 IWD and 1.5 ALSA; A- grade is right. First-pick-caliber in any green deck.
Mistbreath Elder: Sneaky-strong GU Frogs engine — a one-mana 2/2 that either grows or re-buys your ETB creatures every upkeep, dodging removal on demand. 58.1% GIH, +5.8 IWD, ALSA 2.4 all beat its C+ grade badly. A high pick in any blink/bounce green deck, take it early.
Overprotect: Premium green trick — LR's checklist card that "solved every single problem": +3/+3 with trample, hexproof, AND indestructible wins any combat and blanks removal. +4.2 IWD, 58.2% GIH. Numot notes Kenji wheels it, but trust the WR (UP); a high-priority two-mana blowout in any green deck.
Pawpatch Formation: Flexible green staple — LoL's "poor man's Cache Grab": Food + cantrip, or removal for a flyer/enchantment (Talent hate). The modality makes it maindeckable in nearly every green deck; 55.7% GIH and 70% play confirm a high-floor role-player.
Pawpatch Recruit: Strong green rare for GW Rabbits / go-wide. A one-mana 2/1 trample with Offspring that turns your opponent's removal against them by growing your other creatures — punishes interaction hard. ALSA 1.8, 60% GIH, 90% play rate; an early pick that curves out and blanks removal.
Peerless Recycling: Weak filler — the Gift downside (opponent draws first) makes double-recursion costly, and single-target regrowth at instant speed is low-impact. 51.3% GIH, negative IWD, and 41% play rate mark it a sideboard/last-slot card for a grindy BG value deck only.
Polliwallop: Green fight-removal that overkills — twice-power damage one-sidedly kills most things, and Affinity for Frogs makes it dirt-cheap in GU. 85.2% play, but the oh/gd split (53.9 vs 58.4) shows it needs a creature to work. Solid removal-ish playable; premium in Frogs.
Rust-Shield Rampager: Evasive-ish 4/4 for {3}{G} with Offspring — hard to chump-block and flexible into a wide game. Flat +0.7 IWD and 54.4% GIH WR make it a fine curve-topper, not a payoff. C+ role-player; good beater in green aggro, unremarkable but never bad.
Scrapshooter: Premium RG Raccoons/green rare and a great generic body. A 4/4 reach for three is already above-rate, and the gift lets you blow up an artifact or enchantment on ETB — flexible answer stapled to a beater. 57.6% GIH, 2.0 ALSA, 90% play rate: take it early, it's good in any green deck.
Season of Gathering: Green modal bomb (LR A). For 4GG it pumps, blows up all artifacts or enchantments, and refills your hand off your biggest creature — flexible and game-ending in a board-based deck. 60.8% GIH, ALSA 1.6, 89.9% play: a first-pick slam, take it over almost anything.
Stickytongue Sentinel: Overperformer green common — a 3/3 reach for three whose ETB bounce rebuys your own ETBs and, crucially, picks up Talents (Builder's/Hunter's) to replay them, "killing everything." The green card that rose most in the experts' estimation; 55.8% GIH. A strong, flexible early pick.
Stocking the Pantry: Down. A slow +1/+1-counter-to-card-draw engine that LR admits he "picks far more than plays." The 49.2% GIH, -3.3 IWD and 19.6% play are all red flags — too durdly for this format. A niche counters-deck build-around, otherwise a sideboard card.
Sunshower Druid: Solid green common — trending up. A 0/2 for G that puts a counter and gains a life on ETB, feeding GU Frogs blink and providing Forage fodder; LR notes it 'did great work on its own' out of Pond Prophet's shadow. 56% GIH and +3.8 IWD — a reliable early-curve value creature, better than its C grade.
Tender Wildguide: Premium green two-drop and near-universal early pick — a mana dork that fixes any color AND grows into a threat, with Offspring giving late-game reach. 60.9% GIH, +8.0 IWD, 91% play rate. Enables splashes and never sits idle; take it highly regardless of archetype.
Thornvault Forager: Premium BG Squirrels rare — a two-drop mana dork that ramps, fixes any splash via Forage, and tutors Squirrels late. 60% OH WR, ALSA 2.0, B+ grade. Accelerant plus tribal engine plus fixing in one body; take it very highly in green, especially BG.
Three Tree Rootweaver: Quiet two-drop mana dork — a 1/3 that taps for any color, enabling splashes and blocking early. 78.9% play rate; the C+ grade and 54.9% GIH WR reflect that it's a fixer/body, not impactful on its own. Very useful glue in greedy or splash-heavy green decks.
Three Tree Scribe: Solid GU Frogs uncommon. A 2/3 for two that grows a creature every time one of yours blinks/bounces without dying — cheap, sticky, and the engine's payoff. 56.8% GIH with a 4.0 ALSA: a reliable early Frogs pick that also just curves well as a body.
Treeguard Duo: GW Rabbits workhorse — a 3/4 that hands a creature vigilance and a board-sized pump, turning a wide team into a lethal swing or a wall. 'Keeps impressing' (LR); 57% GIH and 87.7% play back it. The C grade is too low. Solid high pick in go-wide green.
Treetop Sentries: Solid green common defensive body — a 2/4 reach that cantrips when you forage, walling flyers while replacing itself. Flat +0.3 IWD and 5.7 ALSA mark it as a roleplayer, not a priority; a fine late include in BG/GW decks with a stocked graveyard or Food to sac.
Valley Mightcaller: Elite green one-drop — the 66.0 OH_WR and 92% play tell the story: a 1/1 trample that snowballs off every Frog/Rabbit/Raccoon/Squirrel entering. 60.4% GIH at a 1.8 ALSA. First-pickable in any green go-wide deck; play it turn one and protect it.
Wear Down: Sideboard only. Gift-a-card artifact/enchantment removal is nearly dead in a set with few relevant targets, and the gift hands the opponent a card. 4% play rate, 44.7% GIH, D grade — one of the worst maindeck cards; board it in only against Food/enchantment-heavy decks.
Alania, Divergent Storm: Trap-ish UR spells payoff — the symmetric 'opponent draws' clause and heavy spell-density requirement make it a build-around that underdelivers. A sub-50% GIH (49.9%) and 36% play rate confirm it rarely comes together; only for a dedicated, expert-piloted Otters/spells deck.
Baylen, the Haymaker: Build-around three-color rare that flops without a token engine — the 30.2% play rate and 51.4% GIH scream 'needs the perfect GW/RWG go-wide deck.' A 4/3 for three colors is a mana cost most drafts can't pay. Trap unless you're deep in tokens.
Burrowguard Mentor: GW go-wide payoff — a trample */* that scales with your board, quickly becoming a lethal threat in Rabbits. 60.6% GIH WR and +5.7 IWD beat the B grade; a snowball body that punishes any wide start. Prioritize in GW; it ends games when you're ahead on creatures.
Camellia, the Seedmiser: BG Squirrels bomb-rare and the archetype's anthem. Grants menace to your Squirrels, tokens off Food sacrifices, and pumps the whole team via Forage — a self-contained go-wide engine. 61.1% GIH, +8.6 IWD, 2.6 ALSA: a premium pick that pulls you into BG hard.
Cindering Cutthroat: Aggressive BR Lizards two-drop (three-mana hybrid) with a bleed-trigger counter and menace pump. A 3/2 or 4/3 that pushes through is fine for aggro, but -1.6 IWD and 53.4% GIH mark it a replaceable body. Curve-filler for Lizards, nothing to prioritize.
Clement, the Worrywort: Strong GU Frogs rare and engine payoff — a 3/3 vigilance that bounces a cheaper creature on every creature ETB to loop your value bodies, and ramps Frogs. +5.2 IWD, 57.2% GIH; the build-around glue for GU blink/bounce. High pick when Frogs are open, weaker splashed.
Corpseberry Cultivator: BG Squirrels/Forage value — a 2/3 hybrid that grows each time you forage, giving incidental graveyard-grind reach. LoL calls it great value in green; 53.8% GIH and 65% play mark it a solid role-player, best when your deck forages every turn.
Dreamdew Entrancer: Bomb for GU Frogs. A 3/4 reach for 2GU that stun-locks a creature for three turns AND draws two if it's yours (blink/steal synergy) — enormous tempo-plus-cards. 65% GIH and a huge +13.4 IWD; a top-pick blink payoff that curves well and is hard to answer.
Finneas, Ace Archer: Strong GW Rabbits/tokens payoff — a two-mana legend that pumps your whole token/Rabbit team on attack and draws cards once you're wide. 60.1% GIH and +6.8 IWD; the B- grade undersells it in go-wide. High pick if you're in GW, mediocre value elsewhere.
Fireglass Mentor: Strong BR Lizards two-drop — trades early, then generates repeatable card advantage as long as you're dealing damage, which aggressive BR always is. 59.3% OH WR (beats drawn), B- grade. A premium aggressive engine in its lane; prioritize when in BR.
Gev, Scaled Scorch: RB Lizards signpost — a {B}{R} 3/2 with ward that pumps your team when opponents lose life and pings on every Lizard cast. 64.7% OH WR and +6.5 IWD show it snowballs when curved out. B grade; a high pick and build-around in Lizards, still a fine two-drop otherwise.
Glarb, Calamity's Augur: Grixis/UBG signpost mythic — a 2/4 deathtouch that blocks anything and gives a persistent card-advantage engine (play lands and 4+ MV spells off the top, surveil 2 to set it up). The set-best +11 IWD confirms it takes over games. Splashy three colors, but a first pick when your mana supports it.
Head of the Homestead: One of GW's best commons (LoL, comp to Cloud Goat Ranger). Five mana for a 3/2 plus two Rabbit tokens is three bodies feeding every go-wide payoff, and hybrid mana makes it easy to cast. B grade, 55.9% GIH, 77.6% play; a reliable high pick in Rabbits.
Helga, Skittish Seer: Build-around Bant mythic, not a slam — needs a big-creature ramp shell to draw/grow off MV4+ casts, and the 36% play rate shows the deck rarely comes together. When it does the +6.0 IWD is real, but the 1/3 body and narrow mana make it a provisional C+; only jam it with a top-heavy GWU curve.
Hugs, Grisly Guardian: RG bomb — an X-spell 5/5 trample that exiles the top X for card advantage AND grants an extra land drop, refueling and ramping at once. 58.4% GIH, +7.0 IWD, A grade. A slam in any red-green deck; huge swing even cast for modest X.
The Infamous Cruelclaw: High-ceiling BR mythic, but conditional. A 3/3 menace for 1BR that free-casts cards off the top when it connects — snowballs fast but needs to keep hitting and the discard cost bites. ALSA 2.3 signals hype, yet 54.7% GIH is only good, not busted; a strong early pick in aggressive BR, not an auto-bomb.
Junkblade Bruiser: Mediocre RG common — a 4/5 trample that swings big on Expend 4, but at five mana with a hybrid cost it's slow for the archetype. 52.5% GIH, +0.1 IWD, and a low 44% play rate mark it a replaceable filler top-end you play when short on bodies.
Kastral, the Windcrested: WU Birds payoff bomb — a 4/5 flyer that snowballs every combat connect into reanimation, anthem, or a card. B+ grade, +6.2 IWD, ALSA 2.9. Elite in dedicated Birds, still a strong evasive body anywhere WU; take it highly and it defines the archetype.
Lilysplash Mentor: GU Frogs value engine — a 4/4 reach body that blinks your own creatures for repeatable ETBs plus a +1/+1 counter each activation. +6.2 IWD and strong 60.5% GD WR reward the grind; the B- grade undersells it. Take it in GU blink; the recurring value wins long games.
Lunar Convocation: WB Bats build-around rare — an enchantment engine that drains, makes flying Bats when you gain and lose life, and turns excess mana into cards. Needs the lifegain/drain shell to fire: the OH/GD split (51.2% vs 55%) marks it as a synergy payoff. Good in Bats, mediocre 53.4% overall.
Mabel, Heir to Cragflame: RW Mice bomb — a 3/3 lord that anthems your team and drops a haste/trample/vigilance Equipment on ETB, immediately threatening lethal. 63.9% GIH, +11.6 IWD, A- grade: a first-pick that wins games on its own. Slam it and lean into aggressive Mice.
Mind Drill Assailant: Niche UB Threshold common — a 2/5 wall that becomes a 5/5 once your graveyard hits seven, with a surveil sink to get there. Outside dedicated UB Rats/Threshold it's a slow blocker (49% OH_WR, 30% play rate). A fine role-player in its home deck, filler elsewhere.
Moonrise Cleric: Reliable WB Bats common — a 2/3 flyer that drips life on attack, feeding lifegain-drain payoffs (Starscape Cleric, Valley Rotcaller). 55.6% GIH and 71% play make it a solid evasive role-player; the body and flying carry it even outside heavy Bats.
Muerra, Trash Tactician: Strong RG Raccoons build-around. A 2/4 for 1RG that ramps off Raccoons and rewards Expend with lifegain and card advantage — an engine that buys turns then pulls ahead. 58% GIH, +6.3 IWD; take it highly in RG goodstuff, though it wants some Raccoon/Expend density to peak.
Plumecreed Mentor: Solid WU Birds engine when built around — each flyer entering grows a ground creature, snowballing an evasive board. Low 41% play rate reflects narrowness, but the +5.1 IWD shows real payoff in dedicated Birds. Role-player: good in WU, unplayable outside it.
Pond Prophet: The card that makes GU Frogs work (LSV's favorite) — a two-mana ETB-cantrip body that's a blink/bounce magnet for repeat value. LR bumped it up; +5.2 IWD, ALSA 4.6. Premium in Frogs, a fine value common in any UG-adjacent deck. Take it as an archetype signal.
Ral, Crackling Wit: UR spells bomb — a planeswalker that self-defends by ticking up on noncreature spells, makes prowess Otters, and refills with card draw toward a storm ultimate. Massive +11.1 IWD and ALSA 2.2 confirm the B+; a top-tier payoff in a real spells deck, mediocre without the density.
Seedglaive Mentor: RW Mice Valiant role-player uncommon. A 3/2 vigilance haste for three that grows permanently each turn you target it — aggressive and sticky in a Valiant-heavy deck. But negative IWD and 53.3% GIH show it underdelivers without target-density; a solid body in Mice, filler elsewhere.
Seedpod Squire: WU Birds filler — a 3/3 flyer that pumps a grounded attacker. Evasion has value but 3W/U for a vanilla-ish flyer is unexciting; 52.6% GIH and 47% play mark it a fringe playable. Fine in an open Birds deck, otherwise a late body.
Starseer Mentor: Strong WB Bats uncommon — a 3/5 flying vigilance that, once your lifegain/loss trigger is online, drains 3 or strips a permanent/card every end step. Great stats (evasive, blocks and attacks) plus an inevitability engine; +2.9 IWD, 56% GIH. A high pick and payoff in WB drain.
Stormcatch Mentor: UR Otters/spells engine — haste, prowess, and a {1}-off cost reducer on all your instants/sorceries, enabling explosive spell turns. 52.8% GIH but only 36% play reflects its narrow home; a strong build-around when you're committed to the spells lane, filler otherwise.
Tempest Angler: Role-player in UR Otters/spells. A hybrid 2/2 for 3 that grows on every noncreature spell — flexible on color but needs spell density to matter, and it's slow to get going. 51.9% GIH, 38% play rate; a fine early body in a committed spells deck, filler otherwise.
Tidecaller Mentor: Conditional UB Threshold payoff — a 3/3 menace that bounces a nonland permanent only with seven cards in the yard, so it's dead early and strong late. 43.5% play rate reflects the narrowness, but GD_WR 58.8% over OH 52.6% shows it delivers in a graveyard-heavy Rats/Threshold deck.
Veteran Guardmouse: Underwhelming RW Mice common — a 3/4 that needs to be targeted to trigger Valiant, and the scry-1 upside is minor. Negative IWD (-1.9) and 44.1% play rate mark it as a filler body; playable in aggressive Mice with cheap targeting, cuttable otherwise.
Vinereap Mentor: Key BG Squirrel/Food signpost — a 3/2 for {B}{G} that makes a Food on ETB AND on death, feeding forage and lifegain twice. 61.7% GIH WR and +7.9 IWD back LoL's "take it." A premium uncommon in BG; grabs value no matter how it dies. High pick.
Vren, the Relentless: UB Rats bomb-rare and a game-ender. Ward 2 protects it, it exiles opposing creatures that would die, and spawns scaling Rat tokens for each one exiled — a snowballing go-wide engine plus soft removal. 60.3% GIH, +10.4 IWD, 2.6 ALSA: take it very high and lean into Rats.
Wandertale Mentor: RG Raccoons two-drop that ramps and grows via Expend 4. As a turn-two mana dork it accelerates and later carries counters — the 63% OH vs 54.7% GD split shows it's an early-game enabler, dead topdecked. B grade, 58.4% GIH; a good early pick in Expend/Raccoon decks.
Ygra, Eater of All: Format-warping bomb — a 6/6 for five with a punishing ward that turns every creature into Food, so it grows two counters off any creature death (yours or theirs) and gains life. Elite 62.8% GIH, +10.8 IWD, 1.6 ALSA (first-picked). Wins on its own; take it over almost anything.
Zoraline, Cosmos Caller: WB Bats bomb — a 3/3 flyer/vigilance that gains life on Bat attacks and reanimates a 3-MV-or-less permanent every attack. 62.2% GIH and +9.5 IWD make it a first-pick engine; the recursion grinds any board to dust in the drain deck.
Barkform Harvester: Filler / changeling glue. A 2/3 reach for 3 that's every creature type and can rebuy graveyard cards — the tribal typing enables synergies but the body and rate are unexciting. Low OH WR and 21% play rate; a defensive role-player that plugs tribal gaps, rarely a real pick.
Bumbleflower's Sharepot: Filler colorless value — a Food on entry with a slow, expensive removal mode ({5} sorcery-speed sac). 52.9% GIH and 34.8% play rate; the OH 48.9% vs GD 55.6% gap shows it's a late-game topdeck. Fine in a slow BG Food deck, unremarkable filler otherwise.
Fountainport Bell: LoL's 'golden egg' — a one-mana artifact that fixes/ramps, cantrips on sacrifice, and quietly enables prowess, Expend, Forage, threshold, and Builder's Talent. Flat IWD but that's fine for a fixer. Include as a 1-of in any deck that cares about artifacts or graveyard counts.
Heirloom Epic: Slow card-draw artifact — a {1} rock that converts creatures/mana into cards, but at sorcery speed with a steep cost. Negative -1.1 IWD and 23.8% play rate mark it a niche grind tool. C filler; only for controlling decks that flood the board, otherwise skip.
Patchwork Banner: Premium colorless tribal glue — an anthem for your chosen creature type plus any-color fixing, playable in every deck. LoL calls it MANDATORY in UR Otters (turns 1/3s into 2/4s) and great in any go-wide typal deck. 59% GIH, 90.7% play rate, 3.1 ALSA — take it early.
Short Bow: Underrated equipment (Numot) — +1/+1, vigilance, reach for 2 with a cheap equip, great at making a squirrel or evasive threat both attack and block. Colorless so it fits anywhere. 52.6% GIH is average but the flexibility is real; a solid role-player in creature-light or pump-hungry decks.
Starforged Sword: Fringe/trap equipment — LR: "expensive, doesn't do much… until they curve out into it." Four mana, needs the gift to auto-attach (handing them a Fish), and strips flying. -3.4 IWD and D- confirm it's below replacement; only a desperate top-end in a creature-light deck. Skip.
Tangle Tumbler: Niche GW tokens payoff — a 3-mana 6/6 vigilance vehicle crewed by tapping two tokens, plus a counter sink. LoL calls it "a beating" in token decks, but the -0.7 IWD and 28% play show it flops without token support. Build-around, not a generic playable.
Three Tree Mascot: Marginal fixing body. A 2/1 for 2 changeling that taps for any color once a turn — helps splashes and counts as every tribe, but it's a fragile filler creature. 52% GIH, 39% play rate; run it when you need fixing plus a tribal warm body, cut it otherwise.
Fabled Passage: Fixing land played in nearly every deck (96%) — enables splashes for a bomb or off-color removal with negligible cost. 56.2% GIH mostly reflects the good decks that run it. Take it as fixing when you need a splash, but it's not a high pick and doesn't advance your board.
Fountainport: Flexible utility land that's nearly free to run — colorless mana with a token-draw sink, Fish maker, and Treasure maker for the late game. 86.5% play, ALSA 3.1. A low-opportunity-cost value engine for token/grind decks; take it as a strong land upgrade in most builds.
Hidden Grotto: Fine fixing land — enters with a surveil and taps for any color at a small cost, smoothing splashes and feeding graveyard synergies. 71.9% play rate; the C grade fits a utility land. Good as a one-of when splashing or in Threshold/Food decks; don't overvalue but happily run one.
Lilypad Village: Trap-adjacent Ub type dual — the doctrine flags the Villages as traps. Adds creature-only mana and enables a surveil ability gated behind a Bird/Frog/Otter/Rat ETB. 53.4% GIH and 42.4% play rate: it enters untapped-ish utility but the color restriction hurts. Only a marginal include in a heavy WU/GU deck.
Lupinflower Village: A trap the doctrine warns against — the type-dual Villages hurt your mana more than the payoff earns. It taps for W (creatures only) and eventually digs for a Bat/Bird/Mouse/Rabbit, but entering untapped and the narrow filter cost you tempo. 56.9% GIH is inflated by good decks; run one at most in mono-heavy white.
Mudflat Village: Above-average type-dual land for UB/black tribal — fixes into creatures and, late, sacs to regrow a Bat/Lizard/Rat/Squirrel. The doctrine calls the Villages traps, but this one's 57.5% GIH and +2.3 IWD reflect low-opportunity-cost inclusion in a black-heavy deck; a fine late pick, not a priority.
Oakhollow Village: A green typal utility land that ramps creatures and pumps entering Frogs/Rabbits/Raccoons/Squirrels — the least trappy of the Villages since it fixes and has upside. 53.9% GIH and 81% play; fine in dedicated green go-wide, but it's still an enters-tapped-cost land.
Rockface Village: Utility land for aggressive tribes — better than most Villages. Taps for R (creatures only) and can grant a Lizard/Mouse/Otter/Raccoon +1/+0 haste, giving BR/RW/UR/RG reach late. 66% play rate and B- grade beat the format's 'Villages are a trap' rule; a fine slot in mono-focused aggro, but the mana restriction stings.
Three Tree City: Trap for typal decks — the fixing is real but comes tapped/slow and it enters producing only colorless, costing you a tempo land in a synergy format that wants to curve out. F grade and 51.8% GIH with a 23.7% play rate confirm it underperforms; skip in most decks.
Uncharted Haven: The premium fixing common for splashes — enters tapped, taps for any chosen color. LoL notes it wheels late. Negative IWD is expected (a tapland). Grab it when you're splashing a bomb like Season or a gold card; otherwise a late-pick mana-base smoother.
Swords to Plowshares: The gold standard of removal — one mana, exile any creature at instant speed, the lifegain drawback trivial in a slow format. Null grade but a 58.7% GIH WR and ALSA 1.8; premium interaction in a removal-scarce set. First-pick-worthy; always maindeck.
Ledger Shredder: Premium blue mythic (a reprint) and a top evasive two-drop. A 1/3 flyer that connives whenever anyone casts a second spell, growing into a card-advantage threat — great in spell-dense UR/WU. 57.9% GIH with a 59.5% OH and 2.3 ALSA: take it early, it rewards a two-spells-a-turn deck.
Rat Colony: Null-data novelty — a 2/1 that pumps per other Rat, with unlimited copies allowed. In a dedicated go-wide Rats deck it can snowball, but you can't reliably draft enough copies in Limited, so the 18.9% play rate and missing WR tell the story. A cute build-around, effectively unplayable as a one-of.
Relentless Rats: Trap/novelty in singleton Limited — a vanilla 2/2 for three unless you draft a stack of copies, which the format doesn't support. Null WR on a 1.7% play rate; effectively unplayable. Take only as a hate/joke pick or if you somehow wheel four-plus.
Kindred Charge: Null data (24% play, no WR) — a six-mana mythic that doubles your board of a chosen type with haste for a one-turn alpha strike. Provisional read: a swingy top-end finisher in go-wide tribal (Rabbits/Mice), but too expensive and win-more to prioritize.
Sylvan Tutor: Null-WR read — provisional. One mana to tutor a creature to the top of your library is a bomb-fetcher in Constructed, but in Limited it costs a card and a draw step for tempo-negative value; ALSA 3.5 shows people pick it, yet 29% play rate suggests it often doesn't make decks. A luxury for decks with a standout creature to find, filler otherwise.
Toski, Bearer of Secrets: Premium colorless card-advantage engine — an uncounterable, indestructible 1/1 that draws a card every time any of your creatures connects, and forced attacking is upside in a go-wide deck. LR's A is right; 56.4% GIH understates it because it must connect. High pick in any creature deck.
Frogmite: LR's 'worst card in the set' — the Frogs deck (GU) has no artifacts, so Affinity almost never triggers and you pay four for a vanilla 2/2. 0.3% play rate, no meaningful data. Unplayable; never pick it, never run it.
Sword of Fire and Ice: Format-warping bomb equipment for any deck — +2/+2, dual protection, and a draw-plus-2-damage trigger every hit. 65.2% GIH WR, +12.7 IWD, ALSA 1.1, 99.3% play rate — the best card in the chunk by miles. P1P1 regardless of colors; it wins games on its own.
Secluded Courtyard: Null-WR mythic land — a colorless fixer that taps for any color restricted to your chosen creature type's spells and abilities. No 17Lands WR, but the read is clear: excellent tribal fixing for a typal deck (enables splashes and multiple pips), a low-opportunity-cost include. Provisional, but play it in any focused tribe.
